title: Skeleton + GitLab CI: pico-sdk/PicoDVI submodules, static 80x30 text on DVI
description: CMake project with pico-sdk and PicoDVI submodules; toolchain.env + scripts/setup-toolchain.sh (pinned Arm GNU, CMake, picotool); scripts/build.sh (build id header, build-info.txt); package.sh/changelog.sh; .gitlab-ci.yml (test/build/package/release) modelled on fz80-firmware. Firmware: libdvi on core1 rendering an 80x30 cell buffer with an 8x16 font, static test screen.
acceptance_criteria: CI pipeline builds a UF2 for the Feather RP2040 DVI; host test job runs; flashed board shows the test screen at 640x480.
notes:
Done (uncommitted): submodules pico-sdk 2.3.1 + PicoDVI dccd738; toolchain.env (CMake 3.31.12, Arm GNU 14.3.rel1, picotool 2.3.1) + setup-toolchain.sh (caches verified tarballs in .toolchain/downloads); build.sh/test.sh/package.sh/changelog.sh; .gitlab-ci.yml test/build(matrix)/package/release; font_gen.py (Terminus 8x16 -> 256-glyph table incl. DEC graphics); screen.c + 8 host tests passing; video.c libdvi renderer; test screen. Local build + package OK. Remaining for acceptance: flash on Feather RP2040 DVI and check test screen; first GitLab pipeline run.
Hardware verified 2026-09-27: test screen displays correctly on the Feather RP2040 DVI; UART0 banner seen on GP0 at 115200 (it was only sent once at boot, so it was easy to miss). Test screen now repeats the banner every 5 s and echoes/counts RX bytes. Only remaining: first GitLab pipeline run.
close_reason: Builds in GitLab CI; test screen and UART0 banner verified on hardware.

title: DVI serial terminal on Feather RP2040 DVI
description: Standalone VT100-style terminal: UART in, DVI out (libdvi, 640x480, 80x30 cells of 8x16), USB keyboard in, UART out. Core1 = DVI scanline render from cell buffer; core0 = UART, VT parser, keyboard, setup. Later a console for a RunCPM compute board. Built with pico-sdk + CMake and GitLab CI modelled on fz80-firmware.

title: Startup logo (power-on/reset) instead of the demo
description: Show assets/logo/ColorLogo-576.png for ~3 s at power-on/reset (not on RIS), ending early on the first host byte or key, then start the terminal. STARTUP_DEMO becomes opt-in (default OFF); STARTUP_LOGO default ON. Design: tools/logo_gen.py (stdlib PNG decode, quantise to RGB222 levels, <=2 levels per 8-px group, RLE) -> generated C; src/splash.[ch] (portable, host-tested) unpacks into full-width encoder rows placed in the idle text raster memory; video.c core 1 splash mode for scanlines 0-575 (status line still from raster), with a blank frame while switching back. RAM: only the compressed table (code/rodata in SRAM).
close_reason: Verified by the user on hardware: logo shows after monitor sync (10 s default, LOGO_MS), ends early on UART byte or key, terminal starts cleanly. Demo is opt-in (STARTUP_DEMO=OFF).

title: Status line vanishes after DECCOLM to the current width
description: DECCOLM (CSI ?3h/l) re-initialises the whole screen including the status row even when the width does not change (vttest, reset/tput init do this); main.c only redrew the status line on a width change, so it stayed blank until a status figure changed. Fixed: term_t.screen_resets counts DECCOLM clears and main.c redraws on it (test in test_term.c). Found by the user during dmt.5 testing.
close_reason: Fixed on branch usb-keyboard: screen_resets counter, main redraws status on change

title: RP2350 build: Pico 2 with the Pico DVI Sock
description: Second stock target pico2-dvi-sock (PICO_BOARD=pico2, PicoDVI pico_sock_cfg: TMDS GP12/18/16, clock GP14). Same firmware at 800x600 / 400 MHz / 1.3 V from SRAM; built and packaged by CI alongside the Feather.
close_reason: Verified on hardware (Pico 2 + DVI Sock) by the user.

title: Cursor invisible on blank cells
description: Regression from dmt.9: raster only counts a cell's fg level where its glyph has ink, so a blank cell's groups hold only the bg level and core 1's cursor inversion (bit flip between the group's two levels) changes nothing. Fix: rasterise the cursor cell as inked (pass the cursor column for the cursor row's slot) and mark old/new cursor slots dirty when the cursor moves (screen_set_cursor).
close_reason: Verified on hardware: cursor visible and blinking on blank cells in terminal mode.

title: 80/132-column modes at 800x600 with startup demo
description: 720x480p60 video (270 MHz); core 0 rasterises changed lines into per-slot pixel buffers (raster.c), core 1 encodes with tmds_encode_font_2bpp + identity font. 80 cols = 8x16 Terminus, 132 cols = misc-fixed 5x8 doubled. 24 rows + status line at 19 px. Demo alternates 80/132 every 5 s until UART0 RX, then terminal starts. Encoder 704 px + pre-encoded black tail (encoder needs multiples of 64 px).
acceptance_criteria: Demo shows both widths legibly with correct colours on the Feather RP2040 DVI; no picture dropouts; terminal still works after the first UART byte.
notes: Moved from 720x480 to 800x600p60 (400 MHz, 1.3 V, COPY_TO_RAM). 80 cols: Terminus 8x16 in 8-px cells, centred (80 px borders) - kept by choice 2026-09-27 (10-px cells considered, declined). 132 cols: misc-fixed 6x13 in 6-px cells. 24-px rows; connector glyphs extend into row padding. Awaiting hardware check and core-1 timing numbers from the diag build.
close_reason: Verified on hardware: 800x600 demo at 80 and 132 columns, line drawing joins. Cursor invisible on blank cells in terminal mode is tracked separately.

title: USB keyboard via TinyUSB host on native USB port
description: TinyUSB HID host on the RP2040 native USB (no PIO). Keys -> VT100 sequences (DECCKM-aware) -> UART TX. Debug moves to UART/SWD. Check Feather DVI VBUS supply for host mode.
notes: Implemented on branch usb-keyboard (uncommitted at handoff): src/keyboard.[ch] portable HID boot report -> VT100 (tested, test/test_keyboard.c), src/usbkbd.[ch] + src/tusb_config.h TinyUSB host (boot keyboards, hub support, lock LEDs), main.c wiring (keys end the demo, status shows kbd). TinyUSB is pico-sdk's nested lib/tinyusb, fetched by CI build job and checked by scripts/build.sh. Needs hardware check: VBUS fed 5V via Feather USB pin / Pico 2 VBUS pin 40, enumeration with DVI running at 400 MHz, keyboard behind hub, LEDs.
close_reason: Done for RP2350: TinyUSB host keyboard verified by the user on Pico 2 + DVI Sock (typing, bidirectional serial). RP2040 Feather crashed with it; USB_KEYBOARD defaults OFF there, follow-up in dmt.20.

title: VT100 parser + screen model with host unit tests
description: Paul Williams DEC ANSI parser state machine (vt100.net). Actions: CUP, ED/EL, DECSTBM, IND/RI, DECSC/DECRC, DECAWM, DECCKM, DA/DSR replies. Portable C with no pico-sdk dependency; host unit tests run in CI. Validate with vttest over agetty.
notes:
vttest findings (hardware, build 50c447b): (1) dark/light background (DECSCNM, CSI ?5h/l) has no effect - not implemented; tracked in dmt.4. Plan: screen-wide reverse flag for the terminal band, applied at rasterisation (swap each cell's fg/bg), all band lines re-rendered on change; status line unaffected.
(2) SGR 4 underline and SGR 5 blink not shown - attributes are parsed into term_attr_t but screen cells have no attribute bits yet; tracked in dmt.4. Plan: per-cell attribute byte in screen_line_t; raster draws underline on the glyph's last-but-one row; blink via a second raster pass toggled by core 0 about once a second (re-render only lines containing blinking cells).
(3) double-width/double-height lines not shown (ESC # 3/4/6 ignored) - filed separately as dvi-feather-terminal-dmt.12.
(4) double-height lines not shown either - split out as dvi-feather-terminal-dmt.13 (builds on dmt.12).
(5) smooth scrolling (DECSCLM) not implemented - filed as dvi-feather-terminal-dmt.14 (after flow control in dmt.4).
close_reason: VT100 parser and emulation implemented and host-tested; checked with vttest on hardware. Findings split out: DECSCNM/underline/blink (dmt.4), double width/height (dmt.12/13, deferred), smooth scroll (dmt.14, deferred), alternate screen (dmt.15), VT52 (dmt.16). REP added.

description: First slice of dmt.6, to validate the flash store (dmt.22) on hardware. SET-UP panel over the bottom text rows, entered with the USB keyboard's F12 (or Pause; the user's QMK keymap has no Pause) on RP2350 builds, or the host sequence CSI ? 999 ~ (then driven by keys from UART RX; hostbridge Ctrl-\). One setting: columns (80/132). Return saves (flash) and applies, Esc cancels. Loaded at boot as the power-on width.

title: Flash settings store usable at the 400 MHz DVI clock
description: SET-UP (dmt.6) must save settings to flash after video_init has raised clk_sys to 400 MHz. Nothing reads XIP after boot today (COPY_TO_RAM; only the copy loader and binary_info live at 0x10000000), but the SDK flash ops re-run the boot XIP setup, and the ROM routines pick their own SPI divisors, so the SCK rate at 400 MHz has to be checked per chip.
design: RP2350 (bootrom source, varm_generic_flash.c): flash_exit_xip -> flash_init_spi -> flash_enter_cmd_xip sets QMI direct mode and M0/M1 to 03h at CLKDIV 12 (BOOTROM_SPI_CLKDIV_DEFAULT), so ROM erase/program run at 33 MHz at 400 MHz: in spec, no change needed. Afterwards the SDK's flash_enable_xip_via_boot2 replays the boot RAM XIP stub (the mode and divisor the boot found at <=150 MHz, CLKDIV >=3, RXDELAY 2), which is 133 MHz+ at 400 MHz. That is only harmless while nothing reads XIP. Fix: xip_retime() = rom_flash_select_xip_read_mode(BOOTROM_XIP_MODE_03H_SERIAL, ceil(clk_sys/50 MHz)) after set_sys_clock_khz and after every erase/program, so settings can be read back and verified. RP2040 (bootrom program_flash_generic.c): flash_init_spi sets SSI BAUDR=6 (66.7 MHz at 400 MHz, no RX sample delay: same failure class as dmt.10), and it is only called from flash_exit_xip ('makes it possible for user code to edit SPI settings'). Fix: own RAM copy of the SDK erase/program sequence (connect_internal_flash, flash_exit_xip, then ssienr=0 / baudr=16 (25 MHz) / ssienr=1, ROM erase/program, flush_cache, re-enter XIP), then set XIP baudr to 8 as well. Both: call on core 0 without flash_safe_execute or multicore lockout (core 1 and all ISRs are in RAM, and a lockout would stall DVI). Leave IRQs on. A sector erase blocks core 0 for 30-400 ms; the serial RX ring absorbs that. Load settings at boot before video_init (the XIP config from boot is valid then). Store: last 2 flash sectors ping-pong, record = magic, version, seq, len, CRC32, data; newest valid wins, erase only the older sector.
acceptance_criteria: Save in SET-UP at 400 MHz on both targets without DVI dropout; settings survive power cycles; read-back verify passes; a UF2 reflash keeps the settings; power loss during a save leaves the previous settings.
notes: Implemented on branch setup-flash (src/nvflash.[ch], settings.[ch]); host tests + both firmware builds pass. Awaiting hardware check on both boards: save at 400 MHz without DVI dropout, survives power cycle, UF2 reflash keeps settings.
close_reason: Implemented (src/nvflash.[ch], settings.[ch]); verified on the Pico 2 (RP2350): settings save at 400 MHz and persist. RP2040 path built and host-tested only, see follow-up.

title: Configurable Backspace key: DEL or BS (DECBKM)
description: Backspace currently sends DEL (0x7f), which suits Linux/macOS hosts (stty erase ^?); a real VT100 sends BS (0x08), which vttest's keyboard test expects and CP/M software (RunCPM) usually wants. Ctrl-Backspace sends BS today. Make it configurable: add DECBKM (CSI ? 67 h = BS, CSI ? 67 l = DEL) in term.c, pass it through kbd_modes_t to keyboard.c (translate(), KEY_BACKSPACE), with tests; and a SET-UP setting (dmt.6) for the power-on default. Found by the user with vttest on dmt.5.
notes: Implemented on branch setup-flash: DECBKM (CSI ? 67 h/l) in term.c with a SET-UP power-on default restored by RIS; kbd_modes_t.backspace_bs; SET-UP 'Backspace sends DEL/BS'. Host tests + both builds pass; needs a hardware check (vttest keyboard test, Ctrl-Backspace inverse).
close_reason: DECBKM (CSI ? 67 h/l) with a SET-UP power-on default, restored by RIS.

title: VT52 mode (DECANM, CSI ? 2 l / ESC <)
description: A real VT100 feature, exercised by vttest and expected by some old CP/M software: in VT52 mode ESC A/B/C/D move the cursor, ESC H home, ESC J/K erase, ESC Y row col (bias 32) addresses the cursor, ESC F/G enter/exit graphics, ESC Z identifies as ESC / Z, ESC = / ESC > keypad modes, ESC < returns to ANSI mode. Needs a VT52 parse path alongside vtparse (VT52 has no CSI and ESC Y takes two raw bytes). Split out of dmt.3.

title: Alternate screen buffer (CSI ?47 / ?1047 / ?1049)
description: xterm alternate screen, used by vim/less/htop (TERM=xterm-color and xterm-16color advertise it via smcup/rmcup) so the previous screen is restored on exit. Needs a second copy of the terminal band's cells (24 rows x 132 cols x 3 bytes, about 9.5 KB SRAM), switching which copy the band shows (plus cursor save for 1049), and clearing the alternate screen on entry. Split out of dmt.3.
notes: RAM budget (RP2040): after dmt.5, __end__ is 0x20039fa4 (24.6 KB heap); boot needs ~14.7 KB heap for the TMDS buffers (video.c), leaving ~9.9 KB. The ~9.5 KB alternate buffer barely fits: measure __end__, and consider trimming TinyUSB (CFG_TUH_*) or the 4 KB rx_buffer. A heap shortfall shows up as a silent crash at boot on RP2040 only.

title: Double-height lines (DECDHL, ESC # 3 / ESC # 4)
description: ESC # 3 (top half) and ESC # 4 (bottom half) of double-height lines are parsed and ignored. On DEC terminals double-height lines are also double width, so this builds on the double-width line attribute and raster path (dmt.12): add top/bottom-half line sizes and, in the raster, double each glyph row and show the top or bottom half (connector padding rows included). Found in vttest on hardware (build 50c447b).
notes: Deferred by user 2026-09-27: finish dmt.3 and dmt.4 first.

title: Double-width lines (DECDWL, ESC # 6)
description: ESC # 6 (double width) and ESC # 5 (single width) are parsed and ignored, so vttest's double-width screens show normal text. Needs a per-line size attribute in screen_line_t (kept when the line scrolls, cleared by erasing the whole line/display as on DEC), cursor movement and autowrap limited to half the columns on such lines, and raster support: each glyph column doubled horizontally (8 -> 16 px at 80 columns, 6 -> 12 px at 132). Found in vttest on hardware (build 50c447b).
notes: Deferred by user 2026-09-27: finish dmt.3 and dmt.4 first.

title: Flash (XIP) build does not start since the 720x480 change
description: With the 720x480 raster pipeline, the default flash-resident build shows no DVI output, and the VIDEO_DIAG flash build prints nothing on UART0 TX, not even 'diag: boot' (the first thing main() does, at 125 MHz before the clock change). The identical code built copy_to_ram works (serial + display). Section layouts match apart from code placement. Board boot2 is boot2_generic_03h, CLKDIV 4. Workaround: COPY_TO_RAM=ON is now the default. Next step: a flash build whose main only blinks the LED/prints, to tell pre-main failure from an early crash; check the LED behaviour on the failing image.
notes: Cause: flash execution fails at 270 MHz clk_sys. boot2_generic_03h (Feather board default) clocks the 03h read at clk_sys/4 = 67.5 MHz, beyond the usual 50 MHz 03h rating; 252 MHz (63 MHz) happened to work. Evidence: a flash build with only main() in SRAM printed 'diag: boot' and 'setting system clock', then hung inside set_sys_clock_khz(270000) (flash-resident SDK code). copy_to_ram builds work; PicoDVI's README builds its apps with PICO_COPY_TO_RAM=1, which is why its 800x600 terminal (400 MHz) runs. Fix: COPY_TO_RAM default ON. Alternative if flash-resident code is ever needed: custom boot2 with PICO_FLASH_SPI_CLKDIV=6 (45 MHz at 270 MHz), set before raising clk_sys.
close_reason: Root-caused: flash SCK over spec at 270 MHz; COPY_TO_RAM is the default.

title: SET-UP screen with settings in flash
description: VT100-style SET-UP on a hotkey: baud, framing, flow control, local echo, LF/CRLF, colours, later VT100/ADM-3A mode. Stored in last flash sector. Shows build id.
notes: Done so far (dmt.23, dmt.18, dmt.26): SET-UP panel (F12/Pause, CSI ? 999 ~), flash store, build id in the title, settings Columns, Backspace sends, Local echo. Remaining: baud, framing, flow control (runtime instead of SERIAL_FLOW_CONTROL build option), LF/CRLF (LNM default), colours, later VT100/ADM-3A mode. Watch RP2040 heap (~19.8 KB after .bss; each panel row saved costs 528 B).

title: Keep the startup logo in flash instead of resident SRAM
description: Nice to have. With COPY_TO_RAM the 19 KB RLE logo (generated logo.c 'data') is copied to SRAM at boot and stays there, though it is only used at power-on/reset; on the RP2040 that is a large share of the ~22 KB heap headroom. Since nvflash_retime() keeps XIP readable at 400 MHz (03h <= 50 MHz), place the logo data in a flash-only section (e.g. __in_flash()) and let splash_unpack (core 0) read it via XIP; core 1 never touches it. Check: RP2040 XIP retime path (depends on dmt.24 hardware check), logo still shows on both boards, __end__ moves down ~19 KB in the RP2040 .elf.map, unpack time acceptable at 50 MHz serial reads.
notes: Implemented on branch logo-in-flash (LOGO_IN_FLASH option, .flashdata.logo section from logo_gen.py). Verified on the Pico 2 (RP2350): logo loads from flash. RP2040 heap after .bss 19.8 KB -> 38.9 KB. Still to check on the Feather RP2040 (with dmt.24).

title: USB keyboard on the Feather RP2040 DVI
description: The TinyUSB host keyboard (dmt.5) works on the RP2350 (Pico 2 + DVI Sock) but the RP2040 Feather firmware crashed with it, even after fixing the boot-time heap shortfall (video.c now mallocs the TMDS buffers). Suspects: RP2040 USB controller bus interface at 400 MHz / 1.3 V (rated 133 MHz), or a TinyUSB hcd_rp2040 panic. Not yet diagnosed: build with -DUSB_KEYBOARD=ON -DVIDEO_DIAG=ON (panic text and HardFault pc/lr on UART0 TX) and note whether it dies at boot without a keyboard or on attach. Until then USB_KEYBOARD defaults OFF for RP2040. PIO-USB (dmt.7) is no alternative at 400 MHz (not a multiple of 12 MHz).

title: Smooth scrolling (DECSCLM, CSI ? 4 h)
description: DECSCLM is parsed and ignored: all scrolling is jump scrolling. VT100 smooth scroll moves the scrolling region up/down a scanline at a time (about 6 lines/s at 60 Hz) and holds off the host meanwhile. Needs: a per-region pixel offset in core 1's scanline -> stored-row mapping (cheap: rows are already per-slot buffers), the emulator queueing scrolls while one animates, and flow control to the host (RTS/CTS or XON/XOFF from dmt.4), since 115200 baud outruns 6 lines/s at once. Found in vttest on hardware (build 50c447b).
notes:
Nice to have, not a requirement (user, 2026-09-27).
Nice to have, not a requirement.

title: HSTX renderer backend for RP2350 boards
description: libdvi has no HSTX backend (PIO + SIO TMDS encoders only). Write an HSTX driver behind the same cells+scanline renderer interface (GPIO 12-19 only). Start from pico-examples hstx/dvi_out_hstx_encoder.
notes: Only RP2040 hardware in use for now; revisit when RP2350 boards come into scope.

title: Optional: keyboard over PIO-USB on pio1 to keep USB CDC console
description: Pico-PIO-USB fully on pio1 (libdvi owns pio0 SM0-2, 6 DMA ch, PWM slice 0). Set tx_ch explicitly (default 0 collides with DVI). 252 MHz is 21x12 MHz OK. SOF IRQ on core0 at top priority. Unproven combination: prototype early.
close_reason: Not viable: 800x600 runs clk_sys at 400 MHz, not a multiple of 12 MHz as Pico-PIO-USB needs, and it would cost more CPU/RAM than the native controller on the RP2040 that already failed (dmt.20). The native-port keyboard (dmt.5) covers RP2350.
